title: Sell Mineral Rights in Ligonier, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Ligonier, PA
metaDescription: Ligonier, a historic Westmoreland County resort town near Fort Ligonier, sits above wet-gas Marcellus farmland. See what that means for area landowners.
heroLead: Ligonier is known for Fort Ligonier and its historic town square, but the farmland surrounding this Westmoreland County resort town carries real wet-gas Marcellus value too.
intro: Tourists come to Ligonier for the fort, the shops around the diamond, and the mountain scenery, and most of them never think twice about what's beneath the working farms just outside town. Those farms, though, sit inside the same Westmoreland County wet-gas window that's kept operators interested in this part of the state for well over a decade, and plenty of local families own mineral interests tied to land their ancestors farmed long before Ligonier became a tourist destination.

sections.heading: Ligonier's Layered Land History
paragraphs: The area's history goes back to the French and Indian War, but for mineral purposes what matters is the more recent chain of title — how farmland around the fort and town square was bought, sold, and occasionally had its minerals reserved as it changed hands over the last century.

Families who've farmed the hills around Ligonier for generations sometimes hold mineral interests that were never mentioned outside the family, simply because nobody nearby had drilled a well close enough to prompt the conversation until recently.

sections.heading: Westmoreland's Wet-Gas Window Reaches This Far
paragraphs: Ligonier sits toward the eastern edge of Westmoreland's most active wet-gas acreage, which means activity here has generally been steadier than explosive compared to townships closer to the Washington County line, but real value still exists for parcels with clean mineral title.

sections.heading: What We Look At on a Ligonier-Area Property
paragraphs: We pull the deed, confirm whether minerals were reserved or conveyed, and check for any lease or unit activity nearby through the Westmoreland County recorder's office in Greensburg before putting together an honest range.

faqs.question: Does Ligonier's tourism economy affect mineral value?
faqs.answer: No — mineral value is tied to subsurface geology and drilling activity, not the surface economy above it.

faqs.question: Is the area around Fort Ligonier actively drilled?
faqs.answer: Activity varies by specific location; we check current unit and lease status for the parcel in question rather than assuming based on the town's reputation.

faqs.question: My family has owned farmland near Ligonier for generations — where do I start?
faqs.answer: Send us what deed or tax information you have, and we'll pull the rest from the Westmoreland County courthouse to see what you actually own.

faqs.question: Does Ligonier's historic district status affect mineral rights outside of town?
faqs.answer: No — historic district designations apply to surface structures and appearance, not to subsurface mineral ownership on surrounding farmland.
